([[Bel Aire, Kansas]]) | college = [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]] (2021–2022) | highlights = * Second-team All SEC (2022) * [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshman Team (2022) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2021]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2021) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2021) * 2× [[Tennessee Mr. Basketball]] (2019, 2020) * [[SEC Men's Basketball Tournament|SEC Tournament]] MVP ([[2022 SEC Men's Basketball Tournament|2022]]) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|FIBA Under-19 World Cup]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2021 Latvia]]|[[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Kennedy Collier Chandler''' (born September 16, 2002) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee Volunteers]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top [[point guard]]s in the 2021 class. ==High school career== Chandler began playing [[varsity team|varsity]] basketball for [[Briarcrest Christian School]] in [[Eads, Tennessee]] while in eighth grade. As a freshman, he came off the bench and helped his team reach the Division II-AA semifinals.{{cite web |last1=Thompson |first1=Khari |title=Briarcrest's Kennedy Chandler poised for breakout sophomore season |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/high-school/2018/12/14/briarcrest-basketball-kennedy-chandler-breakout-sophomore-season-ole-miss/2283196002/ |website=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |accessdate=September 18, 2020 |date=December 14, 2018}} In his sophomore season, Chandler averaged 19.5 points, four rebounds and 3.1 assists per game.{{cite web |last1=Martin |first1=Alex |title=Getting to Know 5-star Briarcrest Christian boys basketball recruit Kennedy Chandler |url=https://www.news-press.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/12/19/briarcrest-christian-boys-basketball-and-five-star-recruit-kennedy-chandler/2689116001/ |website=[[The News-Press]] |accessdate=September 18, 2020 |date=December 19, 2019}} He led Briarcrest to the DII-AA state title, earning tournament [[most valuable player]] honors after scoring 20 points in a 65–54 win over [[Brentwood Academy]].{{cite web |last1=Robinson |first1=George |title=Brentwood Academy's bid to become first with 5 straight titles ends in final vs Briarcrest |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/03/02/briarcrest-upsets-4-time-defending-state-title-holder-brentwood-academy-state-basketball-tournament/3028971002/ |website=[[The Tennessean]] |accessdate=September 18, 2020 |date=March 2, 2019}} He was named DII-AA [[Tennessee Mr. Basketball]].{{cite web |last1=Thompson |first1=Khari |title=James Wiseman, Kennedy Chandler win Mr. Basketball awards |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/03/05/james-wiseman-kennedy-chandler-win-tssaa-mr-basketball-awards/3054417002/ |website=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |accessdate=September 18, 2020 |date=March 5, 2019}} After the season, Chandler won the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] Peach Jam with Mokan Elite.{{cite web |last1=Martin |first1=John |title=How Kennedy Chandler left Memphis (briefly), won a title and became a top point guard for 2021 |url=https://theathletic.com/1101784/2019/07/29/how-kennedy-chandler-left-memphis-briefly-won-a-title-and-became-one-of-2021s-best-point-guards/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |accessdate=September 18, 2020 |date=July 29, 2019}} As a junior, he averaged 22.2 points, 4.3 assists and 2.6 steals per game, leading his team to a state runner-up finish and being named DII-AA Tennessee Mr. Basketball for his second straight year.{{cite web |last1=Biancardi |first1=Paul |last2=Borzello |first2=Jeff |title=Tennessee lands top-ranked guard Kennedy Chandler for '21 college basketball class |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/29661810/tennessee-lands-top-ranked-guard-kennedy-chandler-21-college-basketball-class |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=September 18, 2020 |date=August 14, 2020}}{{cite web |last1=Varlas |first1=John |title=Chandler, Lawson, Cisse all win Mr. Basketball awards |url=https://dailymemphian.com/article/11402/chandler-lawson-cisse-all-win-mr-basketball-awards |website=The Daily Memphian |accessdate=September 18, 2020 |date=March 10, 2020}} Chandler transferred to Sunrise Christian Academy in [[Bel Aire, Kansas]] for his senior season to help prepare for the college level.{{cite web |last1=Thompson |first1=Khari |title=Briarcrest's Kennedy Chandler, nation's No. 1 point guard, transferring to Sunrise Christian Academy |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/high-school/2020/05/29/basketball-recruiting-kennedy-chandler-transfer-sunrise-christian-briarcrest/5280012002/ |website=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |accessdate=September 18, 2020 |date=May 29, 2020}} As a senior, he averaged 14.8 points, 4.2 rebounds and 3.3 steals per game, leading his team to a 21–4 record. Chandler was named to the rosters for the [[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]], [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and [[Nike Hoop Summit]].{{cite web |last1=Lambert |first1=Terry |title=Kennedy Chandler named to McDonald's All-American team |url=https://www.rockytoptalk.com/2021/2/24/22299131/tennessee-vols-basketball-kennedy-chandler-named-mcdonalds-all-american |website=Rocky Top Talk |access-date=June 7, 2021 |date=February 24, 2021}} ===Recruiting=== Chandler received basketball scholarship offers from [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]] and [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]], among others, during his first two years of high school.{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jonah |title=Briarcrest guard Kennedy Chandler building reputation two years ahead of college |url=https://dailymemphian.com/article/4286/Briarcrest-guard-Kennedy-Chandler-building-reputation-two-years-ahead-of-college |website=The Daily Memphian |accessdate=September 18, 2020 |date=April 9, 2019}} He emerged as a five-star recruit prior to his junior season.{{cite web |last1=Thompson |first1=Khari |title=How Briarcrest's Kennedy Chandler went from unranked to five-star prospect in one year |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/high-school/2020/02/28/basketball-recruiting-kennedy-chandler-briarcrest-memphis-tennessee-kentucky-duke/4784748002/ |website=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |accessdate=September 18, 2020 |date=February 27, 2020}} On August 14, 2020, Chandler committed to playing college basketball for [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]] over offers from [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] and [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]]. {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2021}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Kennedy Chandler | position = [[Point guard|PG]] | hometown = [[Memphis, ==College career== In his college debut, Chandler posted 20 points and four assists in a 90–62 win against [[UT Martin Skyhawks men's basketball|UT Martin]].{{cite news |title=Chandler, Vescovi lead No. 18 Tennessee past UT-Martin 90–62 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401371892 |access-date=November 15, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 9, 2021}} On December 4, 2021, he scored 28 points in a 69–54 win over [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]].{{cite news |title=Chandler scores 28, No. 13 Tennessee beats Colorado 69–54 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401371896 |access-date=February 19, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 4, 2021}} Chandler was named to the Second Team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] as well as the All-Freshman Team.{{cite press release|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/33453309/men-basketball-all-sec-teams-awards-announced|title=Men's Basketball All-SEC Teams & Awards Announced |publisher=[[Southeastern Conference]] |date=March 8, 2022 |accessdate=March 8, 2022}} He averaged 13.9 points, 4.7 assists and 2.2 steals per game.{{cite news |title=Tennessee and Michigan play in second round of NCAA Tournament |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/colleges/tennessee-and-michigan-play-in-second-round-of-ncaa-tournament/2022/03/18/11df1a68-a684-11ec-8628-3da4fa8f8714_story.html |access-date=March 19, 2022 |work=[[The Washington Post]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=March 19, 2022}} On April 5, 2022, Chandler declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{Cite web |date=2022-04-05 |title=Vols PG Chandler says he's entering NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33675841/tennessee-volunteers-pg-kennedy-chandler-says-entering-nba-draft-hiring-agent |access-date=2022-04-05 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} Chandler is a projected top twenty pick in the [[2022 NBA draft]]. ==National team career== Chandler represented the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2021 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] in Latvia. He averaged 7.7 points and 3.4 assists per game, helping his team win the gold medal.{{cite web |last1=Butler |first1=Ric |title=Tennessee PG Kennedy Chandler and Team USA Win FIBA World Cup |url=https://www.rockytopinsider.com/2021/07/11/tennessee-pg-kennedy-chandler-and-team-usa-win-fiba-world-cup/ |website=Rocky Top Insider |access-date=July 12, 2021 |date=July 11, 2021}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2021–22 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]] | 34 || 34 || 30.8 || .464 || .383 || .606 || 3.2 || 4.7 || 2.2 || .2 || 13.9 {{S-end}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://utsports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/kennedy-chandler/13426 Tennessee Volunteers bio] *[https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/c/chandler-kennedy.aspx USA Basketball bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Chandler, Kennedy}} [[Category:2002 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Memphis, Tennessee]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[Category:Tennessee Volunteers basketball players]]
